title: The Borrowed Typewriter
premise: In 1946, Yara Nakamura, a pearl diver's child indentured to the Okabe Trading Company, has spent two decades mastering the silences that keep the powerless safe. When occupying forces requisition her island town, they also seize the company ledger containing every diver's true debts and deaths — evidence that could finally free the families or bury them forever. Yara steals a discarded army typewriter and races to transcribe the ledger from memory before the victors' historians write their sanitized record. The book ends with Yara testifying at the inquiry, the typed pages admitted as evidence, and the divers' names read aloud in court — her silence broken at last.
about_author: M. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing colonial trading records across Southeast Asia. They write historical fiction about the people whose names were recorded only as line items.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. We open on the eve of the requisition: Yara keeps the company's books by day and remembers her drowned father's debts by night, practicing which silences keep people safe. When soldiers march into town and seal the company office with the original ledger inside, her mother begs her to let it go. Emotional beat: the cost of survival through silence, and the first crack in it.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Assigned as an interpreter for the occupation administration, Yara sees the ledger crated for shipment to headquarters — proof that will vanish forever. She finds an abandoned typewriter in the requisitioned schoolhouse and begins secretly typing the names, debts, and dive dates from memory, one page each night. A young clerk, Elena, catches her but says nothing. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; found family beginning to form.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Kept
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with Elena's interludes. The transcription nears completion, but the crate ships in three days, and soldiers begin questioning townspeople about 'stolen property.' Elena reveals she lost a brother to a company dive contract and joins Yara, finishing pages Yara's memory cannot reach. When the office is searched, they hide the typescript inside the typewriter's case. Emotional beat: terror and solidarity rising together toward the brink.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the shipping dock, Yara makes her choice: she walks into the inquiry office and requests to testify, submitting the typescript over Elena's forged routing stamp. Her testimony forces the historians to open the ledger on the record; the divers' names are entered into the official transcript. The town hears its own history spoken aloud. Emotional beat: silence broken — grief transformed into belonging, memory made permanent.
